newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Alpi Eagles temporarily grounded.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Alpi Eagles temporarily grounded.

text.p: Italy's aviation regulatory body RAI said on Wednesday it had temporarily grounded private carrier Alpi Eagles pending further safety checks.
"We have suspended the technical airworthiness certificate of Alpi Eagles," RAI director general Salvatore Sciacchitano told Reuters.
"The suspension is temporary and aims to allow technical checks on the carrier's four aircraft to see whether they are operating under safe conditions," he said.
RAI said that during a routine inspection they had discovered technical notebooks of an unofficial type.
Sciacchitano said it was the first time a carrier of Alpi Eagles' size had its certificate suspended.
He said the checks should be completed by Friday.

Alpi Eagles started business in June and is owned by a group of Northeast Italian investors, among them white goods producer Zanussi -- owned by Sweden's Electrolux -- clothes producer Stefanel and the Marzotto textiles group.
